items.headline: Lennart Karl ruled out with torn muscle
items.body: <cite index="1-1">Lennart Karl withdrew injured and was replaced by Assan Ouédraogo in Germany's 26-man squad.</cite> <cite index="1-6,1-7">Manuel Neuer's calf injury kept him out of pre-World Cup friendlies against Finland and the USA, but all indications are that the 40-year-old will be fit to face Curaçao on June 14.</cite>

items.headline: Key players available and ready
items.body: <cite index="1-10,1-11">Jamal Musiala has recovered well from a broken leg suffered at the FIFA Club World Cup and has been getting better with still plenty of time to build up rhythm.</cite> <cite index="14-2">Florian Wirtz has already hit double digits for goals and assists for his nation.</cite>

items.headline: Serge Gnabry unavailable
items.body: <cite index="1-15">Serge Gnabry's injury setback means Leroy Sané could be asked to provide width and pace on the right.</cite> <cite index="18-15">Gnabry suffered a torn adductor and is unavailable for the tournament.</cite>

items.headline: Strong recent performances
items.body: <cite index="12-2">Julian Nagelsmann's side eased to World Cup 2026 qualification with five wins from six.</cite> <cite index="26-2">Germany also performed well as the host nation at Euro 2024, falling to Spain in the quarterfinals.</cite>

items.headline: Club form transitions
items.body: <cite index="11-12">Deniz Undav finished as the leading German scorer in the Bundesliga in 2025/26 on 19 goals, with Nagelsmann stating 'You cannot leave a striker like him at home.'</cite> <cite index="16-4">Florian Wirtz has contributed 15 goal involvements in all competitions for Liverpool.</cite>

items.headline: Optimistic mood heading to tournament
items.body: <cite index="26-5">The mood around the camp has shifted considerably under Nagelsmann, with genuine optimism heading into North America.</cite> <cite index="15-2">The mood around the squad seems optimistic, and they will expect to go deep in the tournament.</cite>

items.headline: 4-2-3-1 formation preferred
items.body: <cite index="11-10,11-11">The lone striker's role in Nagelsmann's preferred 4-2-3-1 formation remains open, with Kai Havertz appearing to be the preferred option when fit, while Nick Woltemade's height and physical presence offer a different approach.</cite>

items.headline: Midfield and defense structure
items.body: <cite index="18-13">Leon Goretzka should link arms with highly-rated Aleksandar Pavlovic in centre-midfield.</cite> <cite index="18-12">Jonathan Tah and Nico Schlotterbeck are expected to form a centre-back partnership in a four-man defence.</cite>

items.headline: Pressing and possession focus
items.body: <cite index="12-11,12-12">Nagelsmann's style relies on gegenpressing when his team lose the ball, while on the ball his teams often try to dominate possession.</cite>

items.headline: First fixture: Curaçao on June 14
items.body: <cite index="19-7">Germany vs. Curaçao at Houston Stadium on June 14.</cite> <cite index="15-17">Curaçao are the smallest nation ever to reach a World Cup.</cite>

items.headline: Second match: Ivory Coast on June 20
items.body: <cite index="21-3">Germany face Côte d'Ivoire on June 20.</cite> <cite index="15-18">The Ivorians, returning to the World Cup for the first time in 12 years, are a dangerous side and boast the likes of Amad Diallo.</cite>

items.headline: Final group game: Ecuador on June 25
items.body: <cite index="21-3">Germany face Ecuador on June 25 in the group finale.</cite> <cite index="15-20">Ecuador are a disciplined, well drilled side who conceded just five goals in 18 qualifiers and could be hard for Germany to break down.</cite>

items.headline: Favorable Group E draw
items.body: <cite index="15-15,15-16">Germany will likely have breathed a sigh of relief when the draw for Group E was made, as on paper they will expect to progress comfortably.</cite> <cite index="22-2">The group consists of Germany, Curaçao, Ivory Coast, and Ecuador.</cite>

items.headline: Redemption mission after recent exits
items.body: <cite index="28-1,28-2">Germany had never failed to advance from consecutive FIFA men's World Cup group stages until four years ago, but Nagelsmann has instilled a new standard into the squad.</cite> <cite index="15-21">Germany will fully expect to be in the knockout stages in a World Cup for the first time since 2014 when they went on to lift the trophy.</cite>

items.headline: Squad strength and championship pedigree
items.body: <cite index="12-2">Germany will be regarded as one of the favourites to progress to the latter stages of the tournament despite recent form in this competition.</cite> <cite index="21-4">The joint-most successful European side in World Cups with four wins, Germany are looking to match Brazil's record of five successes at the finals.</cite>
